title: model-loading-breadcrumbs-alex
content:
Purpose: quick personal breadcrumb log for the late-night model-load break/fix. Not a runbook yet — raw notes, commands I tried, errors, and hypotheses.

Context:
- Trying to onboard a community 30B model into Dedicated pooled cluster for perf tests. Model was uploaded by ops to S3 and an index.json generated by a conversion job. Downstream load fails intermittently across nodes.
- Symptoms: some nodes can load shards fine, others crash during state_dict restore with EOF/unpickling/tensor-size mismatch. Error appears before allocator OOM in some cases.

Commands I ran (chronological):
1) verify S3 objects and sizes locally
   aws s3 ls s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/ --recursive --human-readable
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/ . --recursive --exclude "*.json" --include "*.bin"
   sha256sum *.bin > local-shasums.txt
   cat index.json | jq -r '.weights[] | .file' > expected-files.txt

2) check index.json mapping and total byte counts
   jq -r '.weights | length' index.json  # expected 16 shards
   jq -c '.weights[]' index.json | nl -ba | sed -n '1,20p'

3) git lfs / hf retrieval sanity checks (for vendor uploads)
   git lfs pull --include="models/llm-30b/**"
   pip install huggingface_hub safetensors --upgrade
   python -c "from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download; hf_hub_download('org/llm-30b','pytorch_model-00001-of-00016.bin')"

4) attempted local load with transformers
   PYTHONPATH=. python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
m='local-llm-30b'
try:
    model=AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(m, device_map='auto', trust_remote_code=True)
    print('loaded ok')
except Exception as e:
    import traceback; traceback.print_exc()
PY

Observed errors (snippets):
- EOFError: Ran out of input while unpickling an object
- size mismatch for key 'transformer.h.22.attn.k_proj.weight': copying a param with shape torch.Size([2048, 4096]) from checkpoint, the shape in current model is torch.Size([1024, 4096])
- RuntimeError: unexpected EOF reading file (../csrc/serialized_file_reader.cpp:???)
- safetensors.errors.SafetensorError: index mismatch: file list and index.json disagree
- OSError: mmap length greater than file size
- BitsAndBytes init: TypeError: expected int for quantization param but got str

Notes about errors:
- EOFError and mmap length > file size often mean download truncated or S3 eventual consistency (unlikely but possible with parallel writes).
- Shape mismatch suggests either wrong model config baked into repo or conversion produced different hidden sizes (maybe converted a 20B checkpoint naming as 30B).
- Index mismatch between .bin shards and index.json strongly indicates the conversion step used an incorrect file ordering or one shard got skipped during upload.

Hypotheses / possible causes:
- Corrupted upload: the upload job crashed for some shards and server-side retry only partially replaced files (partial multipart object).
- Index.json refers to a different variant (e.g., fp32 checkpoint vs quantized safetensors) — mismatch between file names and formats.
- Model conversion script (internal convert_to_safetensors.py) used different tokenizer/config mapping, changing expected shapes.
- Shard ordering changed: some nodes read weights in a lexicographic order and others by index.json; if file naming inconsistent (model-1 instead of 00001) you can get wrong assembly.
- Git LFS pointer files left in place (not actual binaries) if someone forgot to 'git lfs fetch && git lfs checkout' before packaging.

What I tried to reproduce and isolate:
- Re-downloaded single problematic shard onto a node that failed and compared sha256: mismatch -> file corrupted on S3.
- Ran `file model-00005-of-00016.bin` and `hexdump -C | head` on both good/bad copies — observed identical header bytes for safetensors ("safetensors" magic) on good but corrupted copy lacked the tail region.
- Created minimal loader to read safetensors header:
   python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; f=safe_open('model-00005-of-00016.bin','rb'); print(f.keys())"
  -> crashed on bad copy with EOF.
- Tried loading with torch.load on .bin -> unpickling error (expected for non-pickle files).

Repro steps for ops to validate S3 integrity (notes to ops team):
- aws s3 cp --only-show-errors --recursive s3://redwood-models/llm-30b/ /tmp/verify && find /tmp/verify -type f -exec sha256sum {} \; > /tmp/verify-shasums.txt
- Compare against checked-in shasums produced by conversion job (artifact in CI). If mismatch, re-run `aws s3 cp` from the CI artifact bucket rather than developer machine.

Temporary mitigations we used:
- Rolled back Dedicated pool to previous model version (llm-30b-v1) and disabled automatic pool routing to the new candidate until we fix source artifacts.
- Put a pre-load check in runtime: for each shard run a fast safetensors header read and file-size sanity check before starting full torch restore. If check fails, mark node capacity degraded and fallback to other nodes. (this is a quick bandaid)

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Ask conversion owner (PR #482) to re-run conversion with following constraints: produce index.json with explicit shard checksums and include a top-level artifact manifest.
- [ ] Add a CI step to validate shard integrity after upload (compare bytes, atomically write manifest file once all shards uploaded).
- [ ] Update onboarding doc with `safetensors` header validation snippet.
- [ ] Fix naming conventions: enforce zero-padded shard names 00001-of-00016 so lexicographic ordering is stable. Add linter in packaging stage.
- [ ] Investigate shape mismatch: add a validator that loads model config (hidden_size, n_layers) and verifies it matches converted tensor shapes before advertising to infra.
- [ ] Create a short playbook for on-call: how to run fast-checks and perform rollback.

Notes to self / random observations:
- One node had slower network MTU and repeated tcp timeouts during parallel downloads; aws s3 cp retried and produced a partial file sometimes (multipart upload conflict?). Could be node-level network flakiness leads to corrupted partial objects saved to local cache path — double-check the client temp file write behavior.
- Consider switching downloads to use `--no-progress --no-guess-mime-type` flags? Not sure helps.

Useful references I found while debugging: 
- https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors/issues/123 (EOF on partial file)
- https://github.com/transformers-team/transformers/issues/4567 (shape mismatch after conversion)
- internal GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 (conversion + upload job)

Slack breadcrumbs: 
- slack thread: #infra-models "llm-30b shards failing on dedicated nodes" (see msg ts: 1689852000.000300)

If I come back tomorrow:
- re-download all shards to a clean EBS volume via aws cli and compare checksums against CI artifact; if mismatch, re-ingest from CI artifact bucket rather than re-running conversion.
- update `runtime` to pre-validate safetensors headers to avoid partial restore crashes; short-circuit and fail fast during model activation so pool routing can fallback.

Quick snippet to validate safetensors header (copy into runtime pre-check):
python - <<'PY'
from safetensors import safe_open
import sys
p=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else 'model-00001-of-00016.bin'
try:
    with safe_open(p,'rb') as f:
        print('keys:', f.keys())
        print('meta:', f.metadata)
except Exception as e:
    print('header check failed:', e)
    raise
PY

End notes: keep this doc informal. When we have a repro and the conversion fix lands, I'll turn into a proper incident report with timeline and RCA.

Last check: re-ran a sha256 pass on node-3 (failed earlier): one shard 00005 differs from CI artifact — flagged for re-upload.

-- Alex C.
